messages.subject: lavaan error (cannot compute p-value when it should???)
parts:
Hi Yves,
  I am fitting the following model in lavaan (this is not a very interesting model, it just arises in a series of models and gives me an error):

SNP.gex.meth.cor <- '
    meth ~ 1   +  methSNP1
    gex ~ 1
    meth ~~ meth
    gex ~~ gex
    meth ~~ gex
'

(I know that the '1' for intercept is not needed, it is just there for a certain reason and should not hurt anything).

Here is the function call:

sem.fit <- sem( model=model.list[[im]],  meanstructure=TRUE, fixed.x=TRUE,
        orthogonal=FALSE, data=lavaan.data, std.ov=FALSE, missing="default",
        estimator="MLM", likelihood="default", information="default", se="robust",
        test="Satorra-Bentler", mimic="Mplus", do.fit=TRUE,
        start="Mplus", verbose=TRUE, warn=TRUE, debug=FALSE )

and here is the error (it cannot calculate the df for this model which should be df=1):
 
Computing VCOV for se = robust.sem ... done.
Computing TEST for test = satorra.bentler ... done.
> fitMeasures(sem.fit)["pvalue"]
Error in if (df < 1 || upper.lambda(N.RMSEA) > 0 || upper.lambda(0) <  :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In pchisq(X2, df = df, ncp = lambda) : NaNs produced
2: In pchisq(X2, df = df, ncp = lambda) : NaNs produced

What am I missing here?

Thanks, Ina

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan error (cannot compute p-value when it should???)
parts:
On 10/15/2014 09:40 PM, in...@vbi.vt.edu wrote:
> Hi Yves,
> I am fitting the following model in lavaan (this is not a very
> interesting model, it just arises in a series of models and gives me an
> error):
>
> SNP.gex.meth.cor <- '
> meth ~ 1 + methSNP1
> gex ~ 1
> meth ~~ meth
> gex ~~ gex
> meth ~~ gex
> '

This looks like a bug in lavaan. lavaan 'thinks' this is a univariate
regression model:

lavaan (0.5-18.733) converged normally after 1 iterations

and calls lm.fit() (instead of the lavaan engine) to get the parameters.
Only, this is isn't just a univariate regression. One way around this is
as follows:

meth ~~ meth
gex ~~ gex
meth ~~ gex
'

now lavaan will see two regressions, and use the lavaan engine (instead
of lm), and everything will be fine.

The lesson for me is that univariate regressions are hard to spot.

Yves.
